entry.evidence: But in the northern Korean Peninsula, geochronology on Cretaceous volcanic rocks has not been yet studied.

sequences.source_document: Yang et al. 2022 published PDF (body) and XML text (abstract, captions)

steps.action: Pose the question whether the undated Mesozoic volcanic rocks of the northwestern Korean Peninsula are Cretaceous, like the Sinuiju Formation, given that no zircon geochronology existed for them.
steps.quote: Therefore, it is necessary to confirm whether these Mesozoic volcanic rocks may be formed in Cretaceous like Sinuiju Formation or not.

steps.action: Take prior age assignments from other work: lithological and paleontological correlation, a K-Ar age of 134 Ma for the Hochon rocks, and U-Pb ages of Late Early Cretaceous strata in NE China.
steps.quote: considered that these rocks were dated to K-Ar age of 134 Ma

steps.action: Collect 36 samples from the Taebosan, Pongsu, Sinuiju and Ryonmu formations and describe their field occurrence and thin-section petrography (Figs. 1–4, Table 1).
steps.quote: of 36 samples, 24 samples and 11 samples were selected for geochronological and Hf isotope analyses, respectively, and 27 samples for geochemical analysis.

steps.action: Measure zircon U-Pb by LA-ICP-MS, zircon Lu-Hf by LA-MC-ICP-MS on the dated spots, and whole-rock major and trace elements by XRF and ICP-MS.
steps.quote: The U–b isotopic analyses were performed using an Agilent7500 mass spectrometer with Geolas200M laser ablation system

steps.action: Check the instruments against reference materials: zircon 91500 as the external U-Pb standard, NIST SRM610 for element correction, and the measured 91500 Hf ratio against literature values.
steps.quote: was obtained for standard zircon 91500, which is consistent with synthetic literature data within error range

steps.action: Infer a magmatic origin for the dated zircons from CL zoning, morphology and Th/U ratios.
steps.quote: which shows that zircons used for U-Pb dating display magmatic origin

steps.action: Take the weighted mean of the youngest age cluster in each sample as its eruption age, giving about 111–107 Ma (Pyongnam Basin), 109.8 Ma (Sinuiju), 118–110 Ma (Jasong), 115–103 Ma (Hyesan) and about 105 Ma (Hochon) (Fig. 6).
steps.quote: a weighted mean age of the youngest age cluster are considered as formation age of volcanic rocks.

steps.action: Retain the formation ages: mainly Albian (113–103 Ma), partly late Aptian (118–113 Ma).
steps.quote: Mesozoic volcanic rocks in the northwestern part of the Korean Peninsula were formed at Early Cretaceous Albian (generally 113–103 Ma)

steps.action: Interpret captured zircons at 125 and 135 Ma as a record of earlier strong magmatism.
steps.quote: The U-Pb data of captured zircons are mainly plotted at 125 Ma and 135 Ma, which meaning strong magmatic event at that time.

steps.action: Infer from εHf(t) and TDM2 that the magma source differs by region: older (Archean) in the western Pyongnam Basin, younger (Paleoproterozoic) in the northwestern Rangnim Massif (Fig. 7).
steps.quote: This means that magma source of the volcanic rocks become gradually changed from older to younger in formation age toward northern areas

steps.action: Report whole-rock major-element compositions, available only for the northern samples, with Harker-diagram correlations against SiO2 (Fig. 8).
steps.quote: Therefore, these chemical composition is represented only in northern margin of Rangnim Massif (block) but no in western margin of the massif

steps.action: Compare eruption and captured-zircon ages with NE China (125–135 Ma volcanics), reading an eastward migration of magmatism to 118–103 Ma.
steps.quote: This shows that magmatism took place farther east at 118–103 Ma, which has been coincided with previous data

steps.action: Take from Xu et al. (2007) the expectation of the lithospheric delamination model: εHf(t) rises as zircon U-Pb ages get younger.
steps.quote: Researchers [Xu et al., 2007], who studied Hf isotopes of Middle Jurassic-Lower Cretaceous intrusive rocks in the Shandong Peninsula

steps.action: Compare the Pyongnam Basin trend, where younger ages carry smaller εHf(t), with the delamination expectation.
steps.quote: ages, the smaller εHf(t) values

steps.action: Reject the crustal delamination model for the northwestern Korean volcanic rocks.
steps.quote: which means that delamination model of crust is unfit to Late Cretaceous volcanic rocks in the northwestern Korean Peninsula.

steps.action: Propose that the TDM2 difference reflects a shallower depth of the Paleo-Pacific slab beneath the Rangnim Massif, where volcanism lay about 100 km farther east.
steps.quote: Paleo-Pacific Ocean Plate subducted beneath Eurasia Continent was at depth shallower than western Pyongnam Basin at that time

steps.action: Support the Archean TDM2 of the Pyongnam Basin with published Archean zircon and crust data from the basin.
steps.quote: lots of Archean zircons including Eoarchean and Paleoarchean were found in the emergences within Pyongnam Basin

steps.action: Retain that the intermediate and acidic rocks form one cogenetic volcanic series, based on similar ages, Hf model ages, REE patterns and linear major-element correlation.
steps.quote: both the rocks would be a series of volcanic product formed in a single environment connected to each other.

steps.action: Plot the samples on published tectonic and magma-origin discrimination diagrams (R1-R2, MgO-FeOT-Al2O3, Pearce granite, Wood Th-Hf-Ta, Th/Nb-La/Sm, La/Nb-Ba/Nb), which place them in arc fields.
steps.quote: These analysed results show that volcanic rocks were formed in island arc setting.

steps.action: Test arc ADR against adakite with two discrimination diagrams; some samples plot as adakites in (Yb)N-(La/Yb)N, but all plot as ADR in Y-Sr/Y.
steps.quote: Some samples belong to adakites in diagram (A) but all belong to ADR suits in diagram (B).

steps.action: Reject an adakitic origin in favour of a normal arc ADR suite.
steps.quote: their geochemical properties being similar to those of arc ADR (normal Island-Arc Andesite-Dacite-Rhyolite) suite rather than those of adakite.

steps.action: Infer from the Archean-Proterozoic Hf model ages that the magma came from older continental crust, not juvenile oceanic crust or depleted mantle.
steps.quote: meaning magma source derived from older continental crust rather than Cretaceous juvenile oceanic crust or depleted mantle

steps.action: Compare the geochemistry and stratigraphy with the Jihei area, Liaodong and Shandong peninsulas and the Yixian Formation (Fig. 17).
steps.quote: this area is well compared with adjacent Jihei area, northeastern part of China but not well with Liaodong Peninsula or Shandong Peninsula

steps.action: Retain the claim that in the Late Early Cretaceous the northwestern Korean Peninsula (with Jihei and Far East Russia) was a continental arc, while western NE Asia was in extension.
steps.quote: Cretaceous volcanic rocks of northwestern Korean Peninsula were in typical continental arc setting at Late Early Cretaceous.

tree.answer: Undated Mesozoic volcanic rocks of the NW Korean Peninsula; their age and tectonic setting are unknown
No; ages and setting are inferred from zircon isotopes and whole-rock chemistry
Date the rocks and infer the magma source and tectonic setting
Partly: arc versus extension, ADR versus adakite, delamination model; mostly implicit in the discrimination fields
Discrimination-diagram fields; εHf(t) trend with age under delamination
Found, not set: rock samples are natural traces
Limited: standards checked; the two adakite diagrams disagree and the authors favour the ADR diagram
Continental arc kept; delamination and adakite rejected

end.claim: The Albian (113–103 Ma) volcanic rocks of the northwestern Korean Peninsula formed in a continental arc setting, which places the eastern part of NE Asia in an arc while western Liaoning was in extension.

decisive_move.sentence: Without plotting the whole-rock data on published tectonic discrimination diagrams there would be no continental-arc claim; the U-Pb estimation (step 7) supplies only the timing.

gates.evidence: The question whether the rocks are Cretaceous like the Sinuiju Formation (p. 1) directed the dating, but no hypothesis directed the sampling design. The ages could have come out Jurassic, and the setting could have plotted outside arc fields; the delamination expectation was tested against the εHf trend. Nothing was fixed in advance, and the adakite conflict between the two diagrams was resolved after seeing the data.

imports.item: Cathodoluminescence imaging on a scanning electron microscope (Mono CL3+)

novelty_claims.quote: But in the northern Korean Peninsula, geochronology on Cretaceous volcanic rocks has not been yet studied.
This magma product has not been defined yet in geochronology in the northern part of Korean Peninsula.

limits:
Sub-claim statuses: the eruption ages (mainly Albian, partly late Aptian) are estimate_with_resolution; the eastward migration of magmatism, the regional source difference and the shallow-slab explanation are best_explanation (the last is untested); the single cogenetic series of intermediate and acidic rocks is best_explanation; the rejection of delamination and of adakite are exclusions.

Coverage of the data: the whole-rock geochemistry that carries the arc claim covers only the northern Rangnim Massif samples (p. 12), yet the claim is stated for the whole NW peninsula.

Internal inconsistencies (inference): Table 1 ages differ from the text and figures for several samples (e.g. 16NK37 111.92 vs 107.1 Ma; 17-SR-8 126.0 vs 124.9 Ma; 18-RT-5 has an age but no U method). Figure numbers in §5.4 do not match the captions.

The youngest-cluster rule for eruption age is applied without a stated alternative or sensitivity test. The prior K-Ar age of 134 Ma for Hochon rocks (p. 2) conflicts with the new ~105 Ma age, but the paper does not discuss this. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded. The XML text holds only the abstract and captions, so body text is located by printed pages.
